#### 1. intellectual disability, autosomal dominant 46  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.484)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-1296072)

**Proposed mechanism:** KCNQ3 (HGNC:6429) —DISRUPTS→ Kv7.2/Kv7.3 potassium channel function (GO:0005305); KCNQ5 (HGNC:6431) —DISRUPTS→ Kv7.2/Kv7.5 potassium channel function (GO:0005305); Kv7.2/Kv7.3 potassium channel function (GO:0005305) —LEADS_TO→ abnormal neuronal excitability (HP:0011216); Kv7.2/Kv7.5 potassium channel function (GO:0005305) —LEADS_TO→ abnormal neuronal excitability (HP:0011216); abnormal neuronal excitability (HP:0011216) —LEADS_TO→ seizures (HP:0001250); abnormal neuronal excitability (HP:0011216) —LEADS_TO→ intellectual disability (HP:0001249). Mutations in KCNQ3 and KCNQ5 lead to haploinsufficiency of Kv7.2/Kv7.3 and Kv7.2/Kv7.5 potassium channels, respectively. The disruption of these channels results in abnormal neuronal excitability, which can manifest as seizures in BFNS2 and intellectual disability in ADID46.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in KCNQ3 or KCNQ5 associated with loss-of-function that do not lead to increased neuronal excitability in functional assays, or demonstration that the pathways regulated by KCNQ3 and KCNQ5 are topologically separate and do not converge on a common downstream effector impacting neuronal function. _(variant: The presence of common, benign variants in KCNQ3 or KCNQ5 in the general population (gnomAD frequency > 1%) that are not associated with either condition would weaken the causal link.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism involving KCNQ channel dysfunction in both epilepsy and intellectual disability could lead to the development of novel therapeutic strategies targeting neuronal excitability that benefit patients with both conditions. For instance, drugs that enhance Kv7 channel activity (e.g., retigabine) could potentially be explored for both seizure control and cognitive enhancement.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in KCNQ3 and KCNA4 in patient populations associated with these diseases do not consistently lead to loss-of-function effects on potassium channel activity, or that the observed phenotypes can be explained by entirely separate molecular pathways. _(variant: Absence of pathogenic loss-of-function variants in KCNQ3 and KCNA4 within relevant gnomAD populations, especially if the proposed disease-specific variants are common.)_
